The bug was in `_cstack` function in `astropy/modeling/separable.py`. When the `right` operand of the `&` operator was itself already a computed separability matrix (ndarray, i.e., resulting from a nested CompoundModel) rather than a `Model` instance, the code filled the relevant sub-block of the `cright` matrix with the constant `1` instead of copying over the actual separability values from `right`. This caused all entries in that block to be marked as `True` (dependent) regardless of the actual separability, losing the correct nested separability information.

Fix: replace 
```python
cright[-right.shape[0]:, -right.shape[1]:] = 1
```
with
```python
cright[-right.shape[0]:, -right.shape[1]:] = right
```

This preserves the correct separability relationships for nested compound models e.g. `Pix2Sky_TAN() & (Linear1D(10) & Linear1D(5))` now correctly returns:
```
[[ True  True False False]
 [ True  True False False]
 [False False  True False]
 [False False False  True]]
```
matching the equivalent non-nested version `Pix2Sky_TAN() & Linear1D(10) & Linear1D(5)`.

Patch:
```diff
diff --git a/astropy/modeling/separable.py b/astropy/modeling/separable.py
index a308e2729..45bea3608 100644
--- a/astropy/modeling/separable.py
+++ b/astropy/modeling/separable.py
@@ -242,7 +242,7 @@ def _cstack(left, right):
         cright = _coord_matrix(right, 'right', noutp)
     else:
         cright = np.zeros((noutp, right.shape[1]))
-        cright[-right.shape[0]:, -right.shape[1]:] = 1
+        cright[-right.shape[0]:, -right.shape[1]:] = right
 
     return np.hstack([cleft, cright])
 
```

Verified with the reproduction script from the issue - the nested compound model now produces the correct separability matrix, and all existing tests in `astropy/modeling/tests/test_separable.py` pass (11 passed).</answer>

args.answer:
The bug was in `astropy/io/ascii/qdp.py`, in the `_line_type` function. The regex used to detect QDP commands (`READ SERR`/`READ TERR`) and the overall line-type regex were compiled without the `re.IGNORECASE` flag, so lowercase or mixed-case QDP commands (e.g. `read serr 1 2`) were not recognized as commands, causing them to fall through to "Unrecognized QDP line" errors, even though QDP itself is case-insensitive for commands.

Fix: compiled the regex with `re.IGNORECASE`:

```python
_line_type_re = re.compile(_type_re, re.IGNORECASE)
```

This allows commands like `read serr 1 2`, `Read SERR 1 2`, etc., to be properly matched as command lines, while the "NO" masked-value check (`v.upper() == "NO"`) and lowercasing of parsed command tokens (`command[1].lower()`) already handled case-insensitivity for those parts.

Verified with the reproduction case from the issue:
```python
from astropy.table import Table
# file contents:
# read serr 1 2
# 1 0.5 1 0.5
t = Table.read("test.qdp", format="ascii.qdp")
```
This now correctly produces a table with columns `col1, col1_err, col2, col2_err` instead of raising `ValueError: Unrecognized QDP line`.

All existing tests in `astropy/io/ascii/tests/test_qdp.py` continue to pass (8 passed).

```diff
diff --git a/astropy/io/ascii/qdp.py b/astropy/io/ascii/qdp.py
index 83a4f004a..768beb0de 100644
--- a/astropy/io/ascii/qdp.py
+++ b/astropy/io/ascii/qdp.py
@@ -68,7 +68,7 @@ def _line_type(line, delimiter=None):
     _new_re = rf"NO({sep}NO)+"
     _data_re = rf"({_decimal_re}|NO|[-+]?nan)({sep}({_decimal_re}|NO|[-+]?nan))*)"
     _type_re = rf"^\s*((?P<command>{_command_re})|(?P<new>{_new_re})|(?P<data>{_data_re})?\s*(\!(?P<comment>.*))?\s*$"
-    _line_type_re = re.compile(_type_re)
+    _line_type_re = re.compile(_type_re, re.IGNORECASE)
     line = line.strip()
     if not line:
         return "comment"
```

def test_rst_with_header_rows():
    """Round-trip a table with header_rows specified"""
    lines = [
        "======= ======== ====",
        "   wave response ints",
        "     nm       ct     ",

    assert tbl["wave"].unit == u.nm
    assert tbl["response"].unit == u.ct
    assert tbl["wave"].dtype == np.float64
    assert tbl["response"].dtype == np.float32

    tbl.write(out, format="ascii.rst", header_rows=["name", "unit", "dtype"])

Fixed the RST writer/reader in astropy/io/ascii/rst.py to accept a `header_rows` argument, mirroring the FixedWidth format.

Changes:
1. `RST.__init__` now accepts a `header_rows` keyword argument and forwards it to the parent `FixedWidth.__init__`. It also recalculates `self.data.start_line` based on the number of header rows plus the two separator lines (`len(header_rows) + 2`), instead of the previously hardcoded value of 3 (which only worked for the single-row "name" header case).
2. `RST.write` now determines the index of the separator ("=====") line dynamically based on `len(self.header.header_rows)` instead of assuming it is always at index 1, so that the separator is placed correctly both before the header block and after it, regardless of how many header rows are used.
3. Updated docstring with a header_rows example.
4. Added a regression test `test_rst_with_header_rows` verifying round-trip read/write with `header_rows=["name", "unit", "dtype"]`.

This resolves the reported issue where `tbl.write(sys.stdout, format="ascii.rst", header_rows=["name", "unit"])` raised `TypeError: RST.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'header_rows'`.

Fixed two case-sensitivity bugs in astropy/io/ascii/qdp.py that caused lowercase QDP commands/values (e.g. "read serr 1 2" or "no") to fail parsing:

2. In `_get_tables_from_qdp_file`, the check for masked/missing values compared `v == "NO"` case-sensitively, so lowercase `no` values (which can appear once the command-line case is fixed) would fail to convert to float.
